dD1: A few JSON keys are a whole project: 640×480, 24 frames per second, 32 frames. check confirms it is valid.
dD2: Sky, sun, hills, meadow, fence and ground marks: layers drawn back to front, with gradients and a sun that blends with Screen.
dD3: Pelvis, torso, neck and two legs with shoes: closed smooth paths with an ink outline. The far side is drawn first and darker, so the near side reads in front.
dD4: Head, ear, hair, ponytail, brow, nostril and a blush. The eye and the mouth are switch layers: open or closed eye, smile or open mouth.
dD5: Each arm is a skinned outline, plus a sleeve and a palm. Every hand has four fingers and a thumb, each a small outline of its own.
dD6: Forty-two bones with parents. Each piece rides its bone, and limbs are skinned with a blend at the joint, so elbows and knees bend smoothly. The dots are the bones.
dD7: Keys on hip, knee, ankle and toes follow a gait: heel strike, flat foot, heel-off, swing. The hips bob. The feet still slide, because the ground does not move yet.
dD8: Arms swing against the legs. The elbows bend more on the forward swing, and hands and fingers trail a little behind.
dD9: Spine, chest, neck and head counter-rotate so the head stays level. The ear and the ponytail follow late and overshoot a little.
dD10: Switch keys choose which eye and which mouth show on each frame. This is also what the lip-sync commands write for you.
dD11: The ground marks and the fence scroll exactly as fast as the planted foot moves back, and the shadow follows the bob. The feet no longer slide: this is the finished example.
dD12: lint runs static checks on the rig and the animation; stats summarises the project.
dD13: The same project becomes a GIF, a self-contained HTML player or a Lottie file.
